mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is a consistent positive predictor of S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, meaning that the observed value of FEDFUNDS always implies positive returns regardless of its level.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows starting from a FEDFUNDS observation.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.5pp) signals monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has risen by more than 0.5pp over the past 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is accelerating (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the market anticipates aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months AND CPIAUCSL > 3.0%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has risen by more than 0.5pp over the past 3 months AND CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When residential investment (RSAFS) growth exceeds 2.0% year-over-year, the economy is in late-cycle expansion, which is associated with overvalued equities and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of instances where RSAFS growth exceeds 2.0% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) is a consistent positive predictor of S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, meaning that the observed value of INDPRO always implies positive returns regardless of its level.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows starting from an INDPRO observation.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, the labor market is tight, which signals strong wage pressures and potential inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) is a consistent positive predictor of S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, meaning that the observed value of HOUST always implies positive returns regardless of its level.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows starting from a HOUST observation.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 (2017=100), it signals a contraction in supply, which is associated with economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls below 100.0.
